definitions: To abandon a bad situation and make it worse by giving up entirely.
To lose one's temper and make a bad situation even worse.
To give up on something and, in a fit of pique, destroy or discard related items.
examples: After the first investment failed, he decided to throw the handle after the hatchet and sell all his stocks.
She was so frustrated with the project that she threatened to throw the handle after the hatchet and quit her job.
Don't throw the handle after the hatchet just because one part didn't work; we can still salvage this.
lemma: throw the handle after the hatchet
source: throw the handle after the hatchet
